title: Lesson 13
subtitle: Telling Time — Hours and minutes
objectives: Tell time in Japanese: hours with じ and minutes with ふん / ぷん
Use ごぜん (AM) and ごご (PM) in front of a time, and はん for half past
Use the particle から (from / since) with times and locations
Use the particle まで (until / as far as) with times and locations
Ask and answer なんじですか (What time is it?) and related Q&A

grammar.title: Saying the hour with じ
grammar.explanation: To say the hour, add じ (o'clock) after a number. Watch the irregular readings: 4 o'clock is よじ (not よんじ), 7 o'clock is しちじ, and 9 o'clock is くじ.
mistakes: Saying よんじ or ななじ for 4 and 7 o'clock — use よじ and しちじ

grammar.title: Minutes with ふん and ぷん
grammar.explanation: Minutes use ふん, which becomes ぷん after some numbers: 1 minute いっぷん, 6 minutes ろっぷん, 8 minutes はっぷん (or はちふん), 10 minutes じゅっぷん (or じっぷん). Others keep ふん: にふん, さんふん, よんふん, ごふん, ななふん, きゅうふん.
mistakes: Saying いちふん or ろくふん — the small っ makes them いっぷん and ろっぷん

grammar.title: AM and PM: ごぜん and ごご
grammar.explanation: ごぜん means both morning and AM; ごご means both afternoon and PM. They are always placed IN FRONT of the time, never after it.

examples.japanese: ごぜん じゅうにじ じゅっぷん
ごご いちじ よんじゅうごふん

mistakes: Putting ごぜん / ごご after the time — they always come first

grammar.title: Half past with はん
grammar.explanation: はん means half past (:30). It always comes AFTER the hour. To say you DO something at that time, add the particle に: にじはんに いきます.

examples.japanese: にじはんに いきます。
しちはんに かえります。
ともだちは じゅうじはんに きました。

mistakes: Putting はん before the hour — it always follows the hour

grammar.title: The particle から (from / since)
grammar.explanation: から means 'from' or 'since' depending on context. It comes after a time or location to say 'from this time' or 'from this location'. It works for both: なんじ から (from what time?), にほん から (from Japan), いつ から (from when?).

examples.japanese: ともだちのいえ から
ごじから いきます。
examples.english: I will go from five o'clock.

mistakes: Putting から before the time or place — it comes after, like English 'from' reversed

grammar.title: The particle まで (until / as far as)
grammar.explanation: まで means 'until', 'up until' or 'as far as'. It comes after a time or location. With location, it marks the final destination. まで and に are different: に is a single destination marker, while まで marks the final destination ('how far').

examples.japanese: ほっかいどうまで いきます。
examples.english: I am going to (as far as) Hokkaido.

examples.japanese: しちじはんまで です。

mistakes: Using に when you mean 'as far as' — まで marks the final destination

exercises.prompt: Match the hours with their meaning:
exercises.explanation: Irregular readings: 4 = よじ, 7 = しちじ, 9 = くじ.

exercises.prompt: What does はん mean when added after an hour?
exercises.explanation: はん means half past and always comes after the hour: じゅうじはん = 10:30.

exercises.prompt: 10:30 in roomaji: juuji ___.
exercises.explanation: じゅうじはん — はん always comes after the hour.

exercises.prompt: にじはんに いきます
exercises.explanation: にじはんに いきます = I am going at 2:30. The に marks the time.

exercises.prompt: Where do ごぜん (AM) and ごご (PM) go in a time expression?
exercises.explanation: ごぜん and ごご are always placed in front of the time: ごご ろくじ = 6:00 PM.

exercises.prompt: ごご しちじ いっぷん
exercises.explanation: ごご しちじ いっぷん = 7:01 PM. ごご = PM, しちじ = 7 o'clock, いっぷん = 1 minute.

exercises.prompt: 1:45 PM in roomaji: gogo ichiji ___.
exercises.explanation: よんじゅうごふん = 45 minutes.

exercises.prompt: How do you say '4 minutes'?
exercises.explanation: 4 minutes is よんふん (yonfun); only 1, 6, 8 and 10 take the ぷん sound.

exercises.prompt: Match the minutes:
exercises.explanation: 1, 6, 8 and 10 use the small っ (ppun) sound.

exercises.prompt: Which is a correct reading for '8 minutes'?
choices: both はっぷん and はちふん
exercises.explanation: The book lists both はっぷん and はちふん as correct for 8 minutes.

exercises.prompt: Build 'It's from 8 AM.'
exercises.explanation: ごぜん はちじから です — から comes after the time it marks.

exercises.prompt: I will go from five o'clock: goji ___ ikimasu.
exercises.explanation: から means 'from' and comes after the time: ごじから いきます.

exercises.prompt: なんじから いきますか
choices: From what time will you go?
Until what time will you go?
exercises.explanation: なんじから いきますか = From what time will you go?

exercises.prompt: まで can mean all of the following EXCEPT...
exercises.explanation: まで means 'until', 'up until' or 'as far as'. 'From' is から.

exercises.prompt: until three o'clock: sanji ___.
exercises.explanation: さんじまで = until three o'clock.

exercises.prompt: しごとは なんじまで ですか
choices: Until what time is your work?
From what time is your work?
exercises.explanation: しごとは なんじまで ですか = Until what time is your work? (Answer: しちじはんまで です.)

exercises.prompt: How are に and まで different when marking a destination?
choices: に is a single destination marker; まで marks the final destination ('how far')
They are interchangeable with no difference
まで is only used with times, never places
exercises.explanation: The book: に can be thought of as a single destination marker and まで as a final destination marker.

exercises.prompt: あおもりけんから きました
exercises.explanation: から marks the origin: あおもりけんから きました = I came from Aomori Prefecture.

exercises.prompt: Build 'My friend came at 10:30.'
exercises.explanation: ともだちは じゅうじはんに きました — the に marks the time something happened.

exercises.prompt: Mini conversation: 'From what time until what time is your work?' — the answer is...
choices: ごぜん はちじから ごご ごじまで です
ごぜん しちじから ごご ごじまで です
ごご ろくじから ごぜん いちじまで です
しちじはんから です
exercises.explanation: From the co-worker conversation: from 8 AM until 5 PM.

exercises.prompt: A friend asks 'なんじの ひこうき ですか' and your flight is 8:17 PM. You answer:
choices: ごごはちじ じゅうななふんです
ごぜんはちじ じゅうななふんです
ろくじはんに いきます
exercises.explanation: From the airport conversation: ひこうきは ごごはちじ じゅうななふんです (8:17 PM). ひこうき can mean 'flight' and 'plane'.

exercises.prompt: Match the から / まで phrases:
exercises.explanation: から = from/since, まで = until — both come after the time word.

exercises.prompt: Until when is your break? yasumi wa itsu ___ desu ka.
exercises.explanation: やすみは いつまで ですか — まで = until.

exercises.prompt: ろくじはんに かえります
exercises.explanation: From the Q&A: ろくじはんに かえります = I will go back at 6:30.

exercises.prompt: Build 'I am going to the airport at 6 AM.'
exercises.explanation: From the drill: ごぜん ろくじに くうこうに いきます.

exercises.prompt: Match the new Lesson 13 words:
exercises.explanation: New words from p.252.

exercises.prompt: Reading comprehension: what time did Samu san come to the Japanese school?
choices: ごぜん じゅうじ (10 AM)
じゅうじ じゅうごふん (10:15)
ごご じゅうじ (10 PM)
exercises.explanation: Samu さんは ごぜん じゅうじに きました — 10 AM. (Jon came at 10:15.)

exercises.prompt: Reading comprehension: until what time is Jon san's arubaito?
choices: until ごご いちじ (1 PM)
exercises.explanation: Arubaito は じゅうにじまで です — his part-time job (at McDonald's) is until twelve.

exercises.prompt: Sentence Building: あした、ごごさんじに にほんに いきます means...
choices: Tomorrow I am going to Japan at 3 p.m.
Tomorrow I am going to Japan at 3 a.m.
Yesterday I went to Japan at 3 p.m.
Tomorrow I am coming from Japan at 3 p.m.
exercises.explanation: The Lesson 13 sentence building sentence: ごごさんじに = at 3 p.m.

exercises.prompt: Short dialogue: Hashimoto san's flight leaves at 9:00. What time does he go to the airport?
choices: ごぜん しちじに (at 7 AM)
らしゅうの かようびに
exercises.explanation: From the dialogue: くじの ひこうきです。くうこうに はじに いきます — the 9:00 flight, he goes to the airport at 1:00.

quiz.explanation: はん means half past and always comes after the hour: さんじはん = 3:30.

quiz.prompt: ごぜん じゅうにじ じゅっぷん
quiz.explanation: ごぜん じゅうにじ じゅっぷん = 12:10 AM — ごぜん goes in front of the whole time.
げつようび から = from Monday. から comes after the time.
なんじですか = What time is it? (Answer: にじ です — It is two o'clock.)

quiz.prompt: Which is the correct reading for 9 o'clock?
quiz.explanation: 9 o'clock is くじ (kuji) — an irregular reading.
Core time words from the New Words list.

summary: Hours use [number] + じ with irregular readings よじ (4), しちじ (7) and くじ (9). Minutes use ふん, which becomes ぷん after 1, 6, 8 and 10 (いっぷん, ろっぷん, はっぷん, じゅっぷん). ごぜん (AM) and ごご (PM) always go in front of the time, and はん (half past) always comes after the hour. から means 'from / since' and まで means 'until / as far as' — both come after a time or a location; に marks a single destination while まで marks the final destination.
